mainTopic: The meaning of 'עד' in רבי יהודה's prayer times, the הלכה for שחרית and מנחה, and rules learned from רב's early שבת prayer.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a question: does רבי יהודה's word 'עד' (until) include the endpoint or not? The גמרא tests this against his time limits for מנחה and מוסף, and concludes that 'עד' means 'up to and including.' His limit for מנחה, פלג המנחה, means the end of the first half of the late afternoon, which is 10¾ hours into the day. רב נחמן proves the same point from a משנה in עדיות, where the morning תמיד was offered at four hours. רב כהנא then rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה for שחרית. Next the גמרא asks who taught that the manna melted at four hours, and shows that both רבי יהודה and the רבנן can accept it. For the end time of מנחה, the practices of different sages point both ways, so whoever follows either view has acted properly. A story about רב praying early on ערב שבת teaches three rules, including that it is prohibited to pass in front of someone who is praying. The amud ends as the גמרא starts to ask how רבי ירמיה could pray behind his teacher, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If 'until' includes the endpoint, רבי יהודה would say the same as the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a proof that 'עד' means 'not including.' If it meant 'including,' רבי יהודה's limit for מנחה would match the רבנן's.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens at the punchline of a proof. If 'עד' meant 'including,' then רבי יהודה's 'until פלג המנחה' would reach all the way to evening, which is exactly what the רבנן say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The late-afternoon period (מנחה קטנה) runs from 9½ hours to 12 hours, and פלג המנחה at 10¾ hours splits it into two halves. If 'until the פלג, including the פלג' means including the whole second half, it ends at sunset, just like the רבנן. Two תנאים are not assumed to say the same thing, so the proof concludes that 'עד' must mean 'not including.'

keyTerms.meaning: The midpoint of the late-afternoon period (10¾ hours into the day)
'Until' meaning up to and including the endpoint

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It finishes a proof that started on the previous amud: if 'עד' meant 'including,' רבי יהודה would equal the רבנן, so 'עד' must mean 'not including.'

phrases.english: That is the same as the Rabbis!
phrases.notes: If 'until פלג' includes the second half, it ends at sunset, which is the רבנן's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that began on the previous amud.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא of the משנה: תפלת המנחה until evening versus until פלג המנחה

steps.title: Rejecting the proof by testing the other option against the latter clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'not including' reading by bringing up the סיפא of the משנה about מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather, what? 'Until' means not including? Look at the latter clause: the additional prayer may be said all day. רבי יהודה says: until seven hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by asking whether the 'not including' option really works. It quotes the סיפא about מוסף to set up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step does not finish the attack yet. It simply puts רבי יהודה's 'until seven hours' for מוסף on the table. The ברייתא and the full argument come in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what? (introduces a test of the other option)
'Until' meaning up to but not including the endpoint
The additional prayer (said on שבת, ראש חודש, and יום טוב)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַאי, עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל?
phrases.english: But rather, what? 'Until' and not including?
Say the latter clause:
And the additional prayer: all day.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: until seven hours.
phrases.notes: The debate is whether this means through the end of hour 7 or only until hour 7 begins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting the proof in Step 1.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'not including' reading will not fit the סיפא about מוסף (shown in Steps 3 and 4).

steps.title: A ברייתא: which prayer comes first when both מוסף and מנחה are due
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא records a dispute. The רבנן say מנחה goes first because it is more frequent. רבי יהודה says מוסף goes first because its time is running out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: If two prayers were before him, one מוסף and one מנחה, he prays מנחה and then מוסף, because this one is frequent and that one is not frequent. רבי יהודה says: he prays מוסף and then מנחה, because this one is passing and that one is not passing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as evidence. רבי יהודה there pictures a moment when both מוסף and מנחה can be said at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is רבי יהודה's reason: מוסף 'is passing.' That only makes sense if the time for מוסף is still open after the time for מנחה has already started. So in רבי יהודה's view, the two time windows must overlap.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Passing (its time is about to run out)
The rule that the more frequent practice comes first

phrases.english: And it was taught:
If two prayers were before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל מוּסָף וְאַחַת שֶׁל מִנְחָה —
phrases.english: one the additional prayer and one the afternoon prayer —

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁל מִנְחָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁל מוּסָף,
phrases.english: he prays the afternoon prayer and afterward the additional prayer,
because this one is frequent, and that one is not frequent.
phrases.notes: מנחה is said every day; מוסף is not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁל מוּסָף וְאַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁל מִנְחָה,
phrases.english: he prays the additional prayer and afterward the afternoon prayer,
because this one is passing, and that one is not passing.
phrases.notes: מוסף's time is about to end; מנחה's time is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the source that makes the סיפא a problem.
steps.raayaObject: That in רבי יהודה's view the times for מוסף and מנחה overlap
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about which prayer comes first

steps.title: With 'not including,' מוסף and מנחה could never overlap
steps.stepSummary: If 'until seven hours' means 'until the seventh hour begins,' מוסף ends at 6 hours, before מנחה starts at 6½. Then רבי יהודה's case in the ברייתא could never happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say 'until and including,' that is how you can find two prayers together. But if you say 'until and not including,' how can you find two prayers together? Once מנחה has arrived, מוסף is gone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the attack. Only the 'including' reading allows both prayers to be available at the same time, as the ברייתא requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה begins at 6½ hours. 'Including' means מוסף runs through the end of hour 7, so from 6½ to 7 both prayers are available. 'Not including' cuts מוסף off at 6 hours, so there is no overlap, and רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא would describe an impossible situation.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find them (such a case can happen)
It is gone (its time has ended)

steps.whatToRemember: The סיפא together with the ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה's 'עד' must mean 'up to and including.'

phrases.english: Granted, if you say 'until and including,'
that is how you can find them,
two prayers together.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ ״עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל״,
phrases.english: But if you say 'until and not including,'
how can you find them,
two prayers together?
Once the afternoon prayer has arrived,
the additional prayer is gone!
phrases.notes: Under this reading, it already ended at 6 hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא to knock out the 'not including' reading.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under 'not including,' מוסף ends before מנחה begins, so רבי יהודה's case in the ברייתא could never happen.

steps.title: But 'including' brings back the problem in the first clause
steps.stepSummary: If 'עד' means 'including,' the earlier difficulty returns: in the רישא, רבי יהודה would no longer differ from the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather, what? 'Until and including'? Then the first clause is difficult: what is the difference between רבי יהודה and the רבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns around and says the 'including' reading has its own problem, which is the one raised in Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each reading conflicts with a different part of the משנה. 'Not including' fails the סיפא about מוסף. 'Including' seems to fail the רישא about מנחה, because there it would make רבי יהודה equal to the רבנן.

phrases.english: But rather, what? 'Until and including'?
The first clause is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבָּנַן?!
phrases.english: What is there between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the reading which survived Step 4 runs into the problem from Step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under 'including,' רבי יהודה's 'until פלג המנחה' would end at evening, the same as the רבנן.

steps.title: 'פלג המנחה' means the first half, not the second half
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's 'פלג' refers to the first half of the late-afternoon period. So 'up to and including' that half ends at 10¾ hours, not at sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think that this 'פלג מנחה' refers to the last half? It refers to the first half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 5 by correcting what 'פלג המנחה' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem assumed that 'פלג' meant the second half (10¾ to 12 hours). In fact it means the first half (9½ to 10¾ hours). 'Until and including the first half' ends at 10¾ hours, so רבי יהודה still differs from the רבנן, and 'עד' can mean 'including' everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think...? (introduces a corrected assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: פלג here means a 'half,' that is, a span of time, not a single moment. The whole answer depends on which half רבי יהודה meant.

phrases.english: Do you think that this 'half of the afternoon'
is speaking of the last half?
It is speaking of the first half,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ דְּהַאי פְּלַג מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a term (which half is meant)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פלג המנחה meant the last half, ending at sunset
steps.terutzMaskana: פלג המנחה means the first half, ending at 10¾ hours, so 'עד ועד בכלל' still leaves רבי יהודה different from the רבנן.

steps.title: Defining the end of the first half: 11 hours minus a quarter
steps.stepSummary: The first half ends and the second half begins at 10¾ hours into the day. That is רבי יהודה's deadline for מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what he is saying: when does the first half leave and the second half enter? From when eleven hours minus a quarter have passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the exact time that marks the end of רבי יהודה's window for מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The late-afternoon period runs from 9½ to 12 hours, which is 2½ hours long, so its midpoint is 10¾ hours. רבי יהודה's 'עד' is therefore 'including' in both clauses: מנחה runs through 10¾ hours, and מוסף runs through the end of hour 7.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he is saying

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, 'עד' means 'up to and including.' מוסף lasts through the end of hour 7, and מנחה lasts until פלג המנחה, which is 11 hours minus a quarter (10¾ hours).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sugya is the source for the halachic time of פלג המנחה (10¾ seasonal hours). That time plays a role in later halachic discussions about the deadline for מנחה and the earliest time for מעריב.

phrases.english: And this is what he is saying:
When does the first half leave
and the last half enter —

phrases.aramaic: מִכִּי נָפְקִי אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר רְבִיעַ.
phrases.english: from when eleven hours minus a quarter have passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the timing behind the answer in Step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה's 'עד' means 'up to and including.' פלג המנחה ends at 10¾ hours, and מוסף lasts through the end of hour 7.

steps.title: Proof from the testimony that the morning תמיד was offered at four hours
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a משנה in עדיות. In it, רבי יהודה בן בבא testified that the morning תמיד was once brought at four hours. This supports reading רבי יהודה's 'until four hours' as including the fourth hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We also learned this in a משנה. רבי יהודה בן בבא testified about five things: (1) we may have a minor girl refuse her marriage; (2) we may let a woman remarry based on one witness that her husband died; (3) a rooster was stoned in Jerusalem for killing a person; (4) forty-day-old wine was poured as a libation on the altar; (5) the morning תמיד was offered at four hours into the day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a משנה to prove that רבי יהודה's deadline of 'until four hours' for תפלת השחר includes the fourth hour itself. Only the fifth testimony, about the תמיד, matters for our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our prayers parallel the daily offerings, so the time for תפלת השחר follows the time of the morning תמיד. If the תמיד was validly offered during the fourth hour, then the fourth hour is still within the time. That shows 'until four hours' means 'up to and including the fourth hour.'

keyTerms.meaning: We, too, have learned it (in a משנה): a formula that brings support from an earlier source
Testified, meaning he reported an accepted tradition (the style of מסכת עדיות)
We have her do מיאון: a minor girl married off by her mother or brother refuses and leaves the marriage
A single witness, here accepted for a husband's death so his wife may remarry
The daily morning offering in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get lost in the first four testimonies. They are quoted only because they are part of the same משנה. Only the last one, the תמיד at four hours, is the proof. Also note: the מנחה and מוסף discussion in the steps just before was a test case for the original question about תפלת השחר (until four hours). This proof confirms the same conclusion, עד ועד בכלל, directly for the four-hour deadline.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical rule that, according to רבי יהודה, one may pray שחרית through the end of the fourth hour.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
We, too, have learned this (in a mishnah).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא הֵעִיד חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava testified about five things:
that we may have the minor girl refuse (her marriage),
phrases.notes: מיאון, which applies to an orphan girl married off by her mother or brother

phrases.english: and that we may let a woman remarry
based on the word of one witness (that her husband died),
and about a rooster that was stoned in Jerusalem
because it killed a person,
and about forty-day-old wine
that was poured as a libation on the altar,
and about the daily morning offering
that was offered at four hours (into the day).
phrases.notes: This is the testimony that serves as the proof

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion just reached in Steps 6–7, that רבי יהודה's 'עד' means 'up to and including.' It applies that conclusion to the original question about שחרית until four hours.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's 'until four hours' for תפלת השחר includes the fourth hour (עד ועד בכלל).
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת עדיות: רבי יהודה בן בבא's testimony that the morning תמיד was offered at four hours.

steps.title: Conclusion: 'until' means up to and including
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the lesson from the testimony: 'עד' includes the endpoint. It then confirms that the lesson stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: 'until' means 'until and including.' Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states what the proof shows and then confirms it. 'Until four hours' includes the fourth hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated שמע מינה means the proof is accepted with no rebuttal. The earlier doubt about whether עד includes the endpoint is now settled, at least for תפלת השחר according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: draws a conclusion, and when repeated it confirms that conclusion
Until and including: the endpoint itself is part of the time period

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, תפלת השחר may be prayed through the end of the fourth hour, because עד ועד בכלל.

phrases.english: Learn from this: 'until' means 'until and including.'
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ ״עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws and confirms the conclusion of רב נחמן's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עד ועד בכלל: רבי יהודה's deadline of four hours for שחרית includes the fourth hour.

steps.title: The ruling follows רבי יהודה because of the chosen tractate
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so שחרית may be prayed until four hours. His reason is that a משנה in עדיות, the 'chosen' tractate, agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, since we learned a משנה in the chosen tractate (עדיות) that agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the proof is in, רב כהנא gives the practical ruling. The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so one may pray שחרית until the end of the fourth hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מסכת עדיות is called 'בחירתא' (the chosen one), and its rulings carry special authority as accepted הלכה. Since the testimony about the תמיד at four hours matches רבי יהודה's view, it tips the הלכה in his favor against the רבנן's 'until midday' view.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion
The chosen one: a name for מסכת עדיות, whose rulings are accepted as הלכה

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling here is that תפלת השחר follows רבי יהודה: until four hours, including the fourth hour. The source is the testimony in עדיות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical basis for the standard deadline of four hours into the day for שחרית.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
since we learned in the chosen tractate (Eduyot) in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the confirmed proof into a practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: תפלת השחר may be prayed until four hours, because מסכת עדיות supports his view.

steps.title: Who teaches that the manna melted at four hours?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves from the morning תָּמִיד to a teaching about when the manna melted and asks who taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding the morning daily offering that was brought at four hours: Who taught what we learned, that “when the sun grew hot, it melted” took place at four hours?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question. It connects the earlier mention of four hours to a teaching about the manna.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning תָּמִיד provides the link to the number four. The question now is which תנא can agree that the manna melted at that hour.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: And regarding the daily morning offering
that was brought at four hours,
who taught what we learned:
“And when the sun grew hot, it melted”—at four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא לְהָא דִּתְנַן:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the four-hour morning offering discussed earlier to a separate teaching about the manna.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא teaches that the manna melted at four hours?

steps.title: The teaching distinguishes four hours from six
steps.stepSummary: A second verse calls six hours the heat of the day, so the teaching places the manna’s melting at four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it was at four hours, or perhaps only at six? When the verse says “in the heat of the day,” six hours has already been stated. So “when the sun grew hot, it melted” is placed at four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted teaching explains how it arrived at four hours. It compares two descriptions of daytime heat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: “In the heat of the day” describes the later, hotter time of six hours. The teaching therefore reads “when the sun grew hot” as an earlier time: four hours.

keyTerms.meaning: in the heat of the day
explain or assign a meaning to a verse

phrases.english: Do you say at four hours,
or is it perhaps only at six hours?!
When it says “in the heat of the day,”
six hours has already been stated,
so how do I explain
“And when the sun grew hot, it melted”? At four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּאַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּשֵׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת?!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the four-hour teaching just introduced.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the manna melted at four hours.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between “וְחַם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְנָמָס” and “כְּחֹם הַיּוֹם.”

steps.title: Neither view seems to fit the manna’s timing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא initially finds a problem with assigning the teaching to either רבי יהודה or רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who teaches it? Neither רבי יהודה nor the רבנן. If רבי יהודה, even through four hours it is morning! If the רבנן, even through noon it is morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges both possible answers to its question. Each view appears to keep “morning” going too long for this reading of the manna.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes that the time allowed for the morning תָּמִיד defines the morning period relevant to gathering manna. If that period still includes the fourth hour—or lasts until noon—why would the manna already melt at four hours?

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Whose view is it? Neither Rabbi Yehuda’s nor the Sages’.
If it is Rabbi Yehuda’s view,

phrases.aramaic: עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת נָמֵי צַפְרָא הוּא!
phrases.english: even through four hours it is still morning!
If it is the Sages’ view—
even through noon it is still morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבָּנַן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the four-hour reading can fit either view of how long morning lasts.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the four-hour manna teaching to רבי יהודה or רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each view allows the morning תָּמִיד at a time when, according to the teaching, the manna has already melted.

steps.title: The רבנן can divide morning into two parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the teaching can fit either view, then explains how it fits רבנן: the repeated word “morning” divides their morning period in two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say רבי יהודה; if you wish, say the רבנן. If you say the רבנן, the verse says “morning by morning”—divide it into two mornings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the challenge. It first promises two possible answers, then gives the answer for רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, morning extends until noon. Reading the repeated “morning” as a division leaves the first half, ending after the third hour, for gathering the manna; melting at four hours can then follow.

keyTerms.meaning: divide it into two morning periods

phrases.english: If you wish, say Rabbi Yehuda,
and if you wish, say the Sages:
If you wish, say the Sages:
the verse says “morning by morning”—
divide it into two morning periods.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבָּנַן:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty concerning רבנן by distinguishing the whole morning from the earlier period for gathering manna.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the repeated word “morning” as splitting the morning period.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If morning lasts until noon, the manna could not melt at four hours.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבנן, the manna can be gathered during the first half of morning and melt at four hours.

steps.title: רבי יהודה can move the gathering time one hour earlier
steps.stepSummary: The extra “morning” can also fit רבי יהודה by ending the manna-gathering period one hour before his morning deadline.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say רבי יהודה: this extra “morning” comes to move it one hour earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now supplies its second answer, for רבי יהודה. The extra word makes the time for gathering manna end earlier than his four-hour morning deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats the fourth hour as part of morning for the תָּמִיד. The extra “morning” lets the manna’s gathering period end after the third hour, so melting at four hours is not a contradiction.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say Rabbi Yehuda:
this extra occurrence of “morning”—
comes to move it one hour earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the promised alternative answer after the explanation for רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses the extra word to set an earlier gathering deadline.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי יהודה still calls the fourth hour morning, the manna should not already melt then.
steps.terutzMaskana: The manna-gathering period can end an hour earlier, after the third hour.

steps.title: Both readings keep the melting at four hours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the shared result of its two answers: the manna melted at four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, everyone agrees that “when the sun grew hot, it melted” refers to four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this difficulty. Whether the teaching follows רבי יהודה or רבנן, its stated melting time remains four hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two answers differ about why gathering ends before the fourth hour. Neither changes the teaching’s reading of when the manna melted.

keyTerms.meaning: and when the sun grew hot, it melted

steps.whatToRemember: The disagreement about the length of morning does not change the agreed reading here: the manna melted at four hours.

phrases.english: In any event, according to everyone,
“and when the sun grew hot, it melted” refers to four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלָּא עָלְמָא מִיהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the common result of the two explanations.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רבי יהודה and רבנן can accept that the manna melted at four hours.

steps.title: Hot sun and cool shade point to four hours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what indicates four hours in the verse, and רבי אחא בר יעקב answers with a description of the sun and shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: What indicates this? רבי אחא בר יעקב said: The verse says, “When the sun grew hot, it melted.” At what hour is the sun hot while the shade is cool? You must say: at four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the verse itself points to four hours. רבי אחא בר יעקב answers that it describes a time when sunlight is hot but shade is still cool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse mentions the sun becoming hot, not the whole day being hot. רבי אחא בר יעקב identifies that condition with four hours.
steps.whatToRemember: The final explanation uses the verse’s picture: hot sunlight while the shade remains cool.

phrases.english: What indicates this meaning?
Rabbi Aḥa bar Yaakov said:
The verse says, “And when the sun grew hot, it melted”—
which is the hour
when the sun is hot but the shade is cool?
You must say: at four hours.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה, if the opening question is treated as the primary move rather than the answer that immediately follows it.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע? אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing agreement on four hours, explains what in the verse supports that precise time.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does the wording of “וְחַם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְנָמָס” indicate four hours?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It describes sunlight that is hot while the shade remains cool, identified here with four hours.

steps.title: Which view governs the afternoon prayer?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks whether an earlier ruling for רבי יהודה also applies to the afternoon prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The afternoon prayer is until evening, and so on. רב חסדא asks רב יצחק: Elsewhere, רב כהנא ruled like רבי יהודה because a teaching in the preferred collection agrees with him. What is the ruling here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the afternoon-prayer dispute. רב חסדא asks whether רבי יהודה’s view is the accepted ruling here, as it was in an earlier discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling had a stated reason: a teaching elsewhere supported רבי יהודה. רב חסדא wants to know whether there is also a settled ruling for this different prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: in the preferred collection of teachings

phrases.english: The afternoon prayer is until evening, and so on.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to Rav Yitzḥak:
There, Rav Kahana said
the ruling follows Rabbi Yehuda,
since we learned in the preferred collection in accordance with him.
What about here?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא מַאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier discussion of the morning prayer to the afternoon-prayer dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the afternoon-prayer ruling follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: No ruling is supplied
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק does not give רב חסדא a ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He remained silent and said nothing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק gives no answer. The גמרא now has to look elsewhere for guidance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His silence does not decide between the views. רב חסדא therefore tries to resolve the question himself in the next step, and Step 22 gives the final outcome.

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: He remained silent and said nothing to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the absence of an answer to רב חסדא’s question.

steps.title: רב’s early Friday prayer suggests one answer
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא points to רב praying the שבת prayer while it was still Friday afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Let us examine it ourselves. Since רב prayed the שבת prayer on ערב שבת while it was still day, infer that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries to answer his own question from רב’s practice. רב prayed the שבת prayer before nightfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the afternoon-prayer period has already ended, an early evening prayer makes sense. רב חסדא takes רב’s practice as support for רבי יהודה’s earlier endpoint.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: Let us examine it ourselves.
Since Rav prays the Shabbat prayer
on Friday while it is still day,
infer from this that the ruling follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַב מְצַלֵּי שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a proposed answer after רב יצחק’s silence.
steps.raayaObject: A ruling like רבי יהודה for the afternoon-prayer endpoint.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב’s practice of praying the שבת prayer before nightfall.

steps.title: A different practice points the other way
steps.stepSummary: The practice of רב הונא and the sages prevents רב’s practice from settling the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: Since רב הונא and the רבנן did not pray until evening, infer from this that the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counters רב חסדא’s proof with another practice. רב הונא and the sages waited until evening to pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their practice points away from using רב’s early prayer as a decisive ruling. The two practices cannot both serve as an exclusive proof for opposite answers.

phrases.english: On the contrary, since Rav Huna and the sages
would not pray until evening,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: infer from this that the ruling does not follow Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה מִדְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַבָּנַן לָא הֲווֹ מְצַלּוּ עַד אוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion drawn from רב’s practice.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רב’s practice establishes one exclusive ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A different group’s practice supports the other side.

steps.title: Either practice is acceptable
steps.stepSummary: With no exclusive ruling stated for either view, one may follow either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the ruling was stated neither like this sage nor like that sage, one who acted like this sage has acted acceptably, and one who acted like that sage has acted acceptably.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the afternoon-prayer question without choosing one view exclusively. Practice according to either view is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב’s early prayer and the others’ later prayer do not establish a single required practice. The conclusion leaves room for both.
steps.whatToRemember: For this afternoon-prayer dispute, the גמרא accepts someone who follows either view.

phrases.english: Now that no ruling was stated
neither like this sage nor like that sage,
one who acted like this sage has acted acceptably,
and one who acted like that sage has acted acceptably.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּלָא אִתְּמַר הִלְכְתָא לָא כְּמָר וְלָא כְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the opposing indications without declaring either practice invalid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Someone who follows either view has acted acceptably.

steps.title: An incident sets up three lessons
steps.stepSummary: רב finishes an early שבת prayer but does not interrupt רבי ירמיה בר אבא, who is still praying behind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב happened to come to גניבא’s house and prayed the שבת prayer on ערב שבת. רבי ירמיה בר אבא was praying behind רב; רב finished but did not interrupt רבי ירמיה’s prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new incident to set up the lessons it will draw next. Notice both the early prayer and what רב did when the person behind him was still praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The account gives two observations: when רב prayed and how he behaved after finishing. The next step explains what the גמרא learns from each part.

phrases.english: Rav happened to come to Geniva’s house
and prayed the Shabbat prayer on Friday.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲוָה מְצַלֵּי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba was praying
behind Rav, and Rav finished
but did not interrupt Rabbi Yirmeya’s prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי גְּנִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב’s early Friday prayer, now through a fuller incident that will support additional lessons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No rule is stated yet; the incident supplies the facts for the next inferences.

steps.title: Three lessons from the incident
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws lessons about early שבת prayer, a student praying behind a teacher, and passing in front of someone praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this: A person may pray the שבת prayer on ערב שבת; a student may pray behind his teacher; and it is prohibited to pass in front of people who are praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out three lessons from the incident. Each lesson comes from a different detail of what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב’s early prayer supports the first lesson. רבי ירמיה בר אבא’s position supports the second, while רב’s care not to interrupt his prayer supports the third.

keyTerms.meaning: in front of those who are praying

phrases.english: Learn three things from this:
Learn that a person may pray
the Shabbat prayer on Friday.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִתְפַּלֵּל תַּלְמִיד אֲחוֹרֵי רַבּוֹ.
phrases.english: And learn that a student may pray behind his teacher.
And learn that it is prohibited to pass
in front of those who are praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תְּלָת:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extracts three rules from the details of the incident.
steps.raayaObject: Three rules about the timing and conduct of prayer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The actions of רב and רבי ירמיה בר אבא at גניבא’s house.

steps.title: The incident supports an earlier statement
steps.stepSummary: The rule against passing in front of someone praying agrees with a statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: It is prohibited to pass in front of those who are praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the third lesson to an explicit statement by רבי יהושע בן לוי. This prepares the discussion of how far that prohibition extends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב’s conduct provided an example; רבי יהושע בן לוי states the rule directly. The next question will test the rule against another observed practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא whose rule is being supported

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
It is prohibited to pass in front of those who are praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the third inference to רבי יהושע בן לוי’s stated rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי’s prohibition against passing in front of people praying.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב’s care not to interrupt רבי ירמיה בר אבא’s prayer.

steps.title: Did two sages pass in front of people praying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the prohibition from the conduct of רבי אמי and רבי אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אמי and רבי אסי used to pass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge: רבי אמי and רבי אסי did pass by people who were praying. At first, their conduct seems to conflict with the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes their passing fell within the prohibited area. The answer must explain how their conduct could fit the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose conduct is cited as a challenge
An אמורא, the colleague of רבי אמי

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי חָלְפִי.
phrases.english: But Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi used to pass.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי חָלְפִי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי יהושע בן לוי’s rule against the practice of two sages.
steps.kashyaTarget: The prohibition against passing in front of people praying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אמי and רבי אסי passed there, their practice appears to contradict the prohibition.

steps.title: They passed beyond four cubits
steps.stepSummary: Their practice does not contradict the prohibition because they kept their distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי passed outside four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי אמי and רבי אסי walked. They passed more than four cubits away, so their conduct does not challenge the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier objection lacked a distance detail. Once that detail is supplied, their passing and the prohibition can stand together.
steps.whatToRemember: The example of רבי אמי and רבי אסי concerns passing beyond four cubits; it does not overturn the prohibition discussed here.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi—
it was beyond four cubits that they passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי — חוּץ לְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת הוּא דְּחָלְפִי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by specifying the distance at which the sages passed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes passing beyond four cubits from the passing prohibited here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי and רבי אסי seemed to pass within the area covered by the prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: They passed beyond four cubits, so their conduct does not contradict the prohibition.

steps.title: How could רבי ירמיה pray behind רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי ירמיה’s conduct and begins citing a statement from רב against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how could רבי ירמיה have acted that way? Didn’t רב יהודה say in the name of רב: A person should never pray—
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now raises a new challenge about רבי ירמיה praying behind רב. It starts quoting a rule that may conflict with his conduct, but the rule is not yet complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer dealt with passing in front of someone praying; it did not address where רבי ירמיה stood to pray. The גמרא turns to that separate issue and introduces רב’s statement as the basis for its challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The person whose conduct is being questioned.
How could he act that way?
Never; here it introduces a firm prohibition.

phrases.english: But how could Rabbi Yirmeya have acted that way?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn’t Rav Yehuda say that Rav said:
A person should never pray
phrases.notes: The quoted rule is unfinished on this amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי?!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 27 resolved the question about passing in front of someone praying. This step opens a different challenge about רבי ירמיה’s position while praying.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה’s conduct when he prayed behind רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא begins citing a prohibition stated by רב that appears to challenge his conduct; the prohibition’s full wording comes on the next amud.
